parts.kar: CURVATURE, one newly assigned bound component

component_law.other_cuts: NONE. Especially oraiin is not or+aiin; qodain and qodaiin are independent whole words. Most recurring strings are unexplained.

grammar.name: Fixed discourse order
grammar.rule: Read N,E,S,W in that order. Printed line breaks do not themselves close expressions. Each case binder starts a discourse episode; no figure mapping is asserted.

grammar.name: Typed application
grammar.rule: A constructor consumes its explicit typed operands in written order. FRAME has WorldRef/View then Station order. No arbitrary scalar/function interpolation or undeclared type coercion.

grammar.name: Case scope
grammar.rule: Case binders write the observer, base station, comparison pattern and observation scope stated in their lexical definition. A View obtains its c only from that open case. A new episode does not copy a physical event or observer merely because its station pattern is reused. An effectful content binder also yields its named nucleus: sain yields Event e, pchedeey yields its introduced star Class. Class binders yield their introduced classes and observer binders their observers. Coordinators combine yielded values of the same sort, not a Case object with a Class object.

grammar.name: Frame and reframe
grammar.rule: FRAME(x,f,c)=View(x,f,c). FRAME(View(x,f,c),g,c)=View(x,g,c), retaining x,c and the inner expression node. Reframing does not physically move the case observer. Two different frames are not two different eclipses.

grammar.name: Two-place report pairing
grammar.rule: A two-node nested view chain lists its inner view then outer view. Two juxtaposed complete views list themselves in written order. Exactly two following report values zip onto that list. Event views require NightPhase; Class views require visibility-report values. No report value can replace a referent.

grammar.name: Event identity and phase
grammar.rule: The lunar-case binder has one e, a whole-event report scope and a local-night phase-report channel. It does not select an eclipse contact or assert exact duration. Approximate third remains approximate. Each local-night phase report owns its local night context at that station; subsequent SUNSET and NIGHT_BEGINNING refer to those reported nights. This is an explicit context-bearing phase-report choice, not a new calendar date or common eclipse contact.

grammar.name: Event-kind order
grammar.rule: EventKind then EARLIER uses the currently written comparison-frame pair. Within a comparison episode this is a complete order proposition; NIGHT_BEGINNING and SUNSET are separately named event kinds.

grammar.name: References and cause
grammar.rule: PREVIOUS_PROPOSITION takes the immediately preceding complete proposition; CURRENT_REPORT_DIFFERENCE takes the episode comparison contrast. A CAUSES B is the infix causal clause. Aspect, proposition and event-kind propositions are admissible cause/result sorts; their owners remain explicit. The report-difference reference yields a contrast Proposition, not a numerical quantity; its use as a causal result therefore does not coerce a scalar into a proposition.

grammar.name: Ultimate-cause closure
grammar.rule: [Aspect] ULTIMATE_CAUSE [optional ONLY] scopes over the open argument episode reports, closes subordinate branches, and attributes an ultimate cause. It preserves nested intermediate explanations. The marker has exactly the same scope rule at N and W; it is not freely attached to a chosen sentence.

grammar.name: Class/event-kind comparison
grammar.rule: Coordinated class introductions establish the current collective topic. A following list of rising/setting kinds followed by EARLIER f THAN g compares those kinds for that topic. Quantification is over applicable rising/setting event cases; it does not assert every star rises and sets at every station.

grammar.name: Earth aspects and one internal cut
grammar.rule: EARTH_ASPECT(k)=Aspect(g,k) with g from EARTH. Permit exactly olkar=ol+kar, kar:CURVATURE. All other forms, including oraiin, olaiin, oloqorain and olchey, are opaque unless separately assigned. No prefix stripping law.

grammar.name: Postfix causal relation
grammar.rule: A B CAUSES has the same relation and argument order as A CAUSES B when A is Aspect and B ReportDifference. This second surface order is an added syntactic freedom, not derived from English or Latin.

grammar.name: Flatness counterfactual
grammar.rule: IF FLAT Axis THEN [station AS_SOON station EventKind] forms CF(Flat(g,Axis), SameOrder(EventKind,f1,f2)). The episode supplies its already named celestial topic; no positive actual flatness is asserted.

grammar.name: Falsity reference
grammar.rule: FALSE CONSEQUENT_REF asserts actual falsity of the previous complete positive consequent, outside the counterfactual. It does not assert NOT(CF).

grammar.name: Evidence projection
grammar.rule: THEREFORE WorldRef INDICATES GroundProperty means the explicitly recorded report history for that WorldRef in the current episode supports that property. Count this report-history projection; do not silently identify a body with an argument.

grammar.name: Two-class introduction
grammar.rule: NORTHERN_CASE followed by ClassBinder AND ClassBinder creates ordered nonempty primary p and secondary q. They are different source-selected classes, not entire hemispheres, and the northern observer need not be the eclipse observer.

grammar.name: Cyclic reports
grammar.rule: View(class,f,c) [ALWAYS] VisibilityProperty gives a class visibility report. With no ALWAYS, VISIBLE means visible during some part of the declared cycle; HIDDEN means no visibility in it. ALWAYS means throughout the cycle for each class member. NEVER_VISIBLE is the corresponding negative cycle value.

grammar.name: Explicit substantivization
grammar.rule: Only in a required WorldRef/ClassRef operand slot, a VisibilityProperty may be substantivized as PrimaryClass(c) restricted by that property at the episode base station. The primary class is fixed by G16, not chosen after seeing a desired result. In a report slot the same token remains the property. This is an extra anaphoric nominalization law, with a base-property presupposition; no arbitrary earlier referent search is licensed.

grammar.name: Topic and same-frame continuation
grammar.rule: OTHER_CLASS_TOPIC changes the current WorldRef to q, but does not change the primary p. SAME_STATION WorldRef ReportValue repeats exactly the previous complete visibility report station and scope. Completion of a FRAME expression updates the current WorldRef to its explicit referent.

grammar.name: Guarded forward travel
grammar.rule: IF TravelExtent TRAVEL opens a prospective branch for the current explicitly bound observer. The extent supplies the direction and sufficiency condition; a destination frame is introduced only inside that branch. All following reports retain the guard until a declared closer.

grammar.name: Prospective tendency
grammar.rule: View TENDS_TOWARD_SETTING reports a prospective tendency in the case regime. It does not imply the class actually completed setting. A CaseRef Subject TENDS_TOWARD_SETTING uses G29 rather than inheriting an arbitrary current observer.

grammar.name: Further travel and qualitative degree
grammar.rule: FARTHER_TRAVEL Direction AND MORE SETTING_TENDENCY_OF ClassRef extends the guarded forward case to a farther frame and compares that class tendency with the preceding written destination. The comparison is qualitative; it introduces no speed, threshold, angular depth or counted stars. The explicit further-travel predication and the MORE comparison each yield a guarded Proposition; AND coordinates those two propositions while retaining the travel update for the second. It is not coordination of a raw event with a degree.

grammar.name: Before/after report construction
grammar.rule: OTHER_CLASS_TOPIC SAME_TRAVELLER HIDDEN NOW CAN_BE_VISIBLE asserts the same named class hidden at that traveller's base station and potentially visible at the guarded forward destination. NOW is case-relative, never a new actual time. The generic template is Topic ObserverRef Property NOW ModalProperty.

grammar.name: Converse and fresh observer
grammar.rule: CONVERSE_CASE ObserverBinder FROM_direction TOWARD_direction TRAVEL opens a subordinate reversed-route case with that new observer. It preserves class identities, not physical person identity. Its guard realizes the preceding possible visibility case, so the reverse comparison does not silently turn mere possibility into an unconditional fact.

grammar.name: Anaphors in paired converse reports
grammar.rule: CURRENT_WORLD_REF and CURRENT_CLASS_REF take the currently named secondary q until an explicit new topic or completed view changes it. AFTER/BEFORE_JOURNEY_STATION point to the active converse journey endpoints. Paired report construction G05 applies unchanged.

grammar.name: Source-selected class witness
grammar.rule: For this synopsis q is a source-selected formerly hidden class that can become visible after sufficiently far southward travel. This aligns the C3 and C5 witnesses. It does not claim every opposite-polar star becomes visible. Count this witness-selection/quantification choice; source wording permits but does not uniquely demand it.

grammar.name: Causal episode and branch retention
grammar.rule: Ultimate-cause closure preserves the recorded forward and converse reports and their conditional scopes as objects of explanation. Closing a branch does not assert its antecedent actually occurred.

grammar.name: Reference to earlier case
grammar.rule: FORWARD_DESTINATION_CASE returns the latest explicitly written forward destination together with its observer, cyclic scope and guard. It never means the current converse state. This is an openly assigned discourse-reference value.

grammar.name: Case-topic report
grammar.rule: CaseRef Subject Predicate forms Predicate(View(Subject,CaseRef.station,CaseRef.scope)) under CaseRef.guard and observer. This is a second, explicit surface construction for a frame-scoped report, with a complete CaseRef operand; no unowned scope transfer.

grammar.name: Counterfactual with actual-status annotation
grammar.rule: IF GroundProperty [ClassTopic] ACTUALLY_FALSE [ReportValue FRAME(WorldRef,ANY_STATION)] forms CF(GroundProperty,P) AND ActualFalse(P), where P is the positive universally stationed report. The class topic sets CURRENT_WORLD_REF before the FRAME. The status projects outside IF by this explicit law, not by silently changing negation scope.

grammar.name: Earth appearance cause
grammar.rule: EARTH_ASPECT(GREAT_SIZE) CAUSES EARTH_ASPECT(APPARENT_FLATNESS) is a ground-body appearance clause. Generic human perception is part of APPARENT_FLATNESS, not the stellar VIEW sort; it does not assert Earth is physically flat.

grammar.name: Visibility property predicates and existential modality
grammar.rule: Class visibility reports distribute over the source-selected class members at the stated cyclic scope. CAN_BE_VISIBLE introduces an accessible destination regime under the travel guard, not an actual sighting. The converse branch is conditional on such a regime, as stated by G24.

clauses.reading: One lunar eclipse: its report here is at the first hour of night, and the report of that same eclipse farther east is at about the third hour.
Sunset is earlier there.
Night begins earlier there.
That earlier beginning of night explains the difference between the reports.
The Earth: its curvature is the only ultimate cause attributed to this comparison.
Consider stars and signs.

source_departures_and_condensation.detail: The Latin infers earlier night/sunset from the differing eclipse reports. N4 explicitly makes earlier local night the intermediate explanation for the report contrast. This is a plausible analytical reversal/elaboration, not a literally stated Latin causal clause.

N5 allows the written intermediate night-beginning explanation while attributing the sole ultimate cause to Earth curvature. The source says curvature alone is the cause; it does not itself label a hierarchy of ultimate versus intermediate causes.

The secondary class consists of a source-selected formerly hidden set that can become visible on the stipulated southward journey. It is not every opposite-polar star, and a choice of witness subset is not a discovered target reference.

The source says the converse happens to someone travelling south-to-north, without spelling out a realized forward visibility condition. G24 makes that condition explicit so modal possibility is not silently changed to unconditional observation.

The travel reports concern compatible prospective cyclic regimes, not an actual dated journey, a completed stellar setting, a numerical threshold, speed or angle. All guards remain attached after causal scope closure.
The three-token final part of W.21 restates the already written forward-case tendency at its preserved case, to respect the repeated fixed qodaiin. It adds no independent source argument.

The source introduces its eclipse illustration with a general remark that this is clear from happenings aloft. The synopsis does not assign a separate ABOVE/ALOFT word or preserve that rhetorical connector. All eight fixed substantive obligations remain represented; this is not complete literal source equivalence.
Eclipse proof precedes the general rise/set proposition; the travel cause and a forward-case reminder occur in W. No additional source unit is adopted.
